name: Step Jack
steps: The Step Jack is a low-impact plyometric-style move that provides cardiovascular benefits without the joint stress of jumping. It works the entire body, specifically targeting the legs, core, and shoulders. This move is ideal for beginners, individuals with joint sensitivities, or as a dynamic warm-up to gradually elevate the heart rate.
Notes (Instructions):
​Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
​Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms up above your head.
Bring your right foot back to the center and lower your arms.
​Immediately repeat the movement, stepping out with your left foot.
​Continue alternating sides at a steady, rhythmic pace.
stepsEs: El Step Jack es un movimiento de bajo impacto al estilo pliométrico que ofrece beneficios cardiovasculares sin el estrés articular del salto. Trabaja todo el cuerpo y se centra especialmente en las piernas, el core y los hombros. Este movimiento es ideal para principiantes, para personas con articulaciones sensibles o como calentamiento dinámico para elevar la frecuencia cardíaca de forma gradual.
Notas (Instrucciones):
Ponte de pie erguido con los pies juntos y los brazos a los lados.
Da un paso hacia el lado con el pie derecho mientras subes ambos brazos por encima de la cabeza al mismo tiempo.
Lleva el pie derecho de vuelta al centro y baja los brazos.
Repite el movimiento de inmediato, dando un paso hacia el lado con el pie izquierdo.
Continúa alternando los lados a un ritmo constante y rítmico.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Slow Squat
steps: ​A tempo-based squat that uses controlled movement to increase muscle tension and improve lower-body stability.
​Lower: Descend slowly for 3 seconds.
​Pause: Hold at the bottom for 1 second.
​Stand: Return to the starting position at a normal pace.
Form: Keep your chest up and weight in your heels.
stepsEs: Una sentadilla basada en el tempo que utiliza un movimiento controlado para aumentar la tensión muscular y mejorar la estabilidad del tren inferior.
Bajada: Desciende lentamente durante 3 segundos.
Pausa: Mantén la posición abajo durante 1 segundo.
Subida: Vuelve a la posición inicial a un ritmo normal.
Técnica: Mantén el pecho erguido y el peso sobre los talones.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Wide Push-Up
steps: ​A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to increase the emphasis on the outer chest muscles and shoulders.
​Setup: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Lower: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your core tight.
​Push: Drive through your palms to return to the start position.
​Form: Don't let your lower back sag; keep a straight line from head to heels.
stepsEs: Una variante de la flexión con una colocación de manos más amplia para aumentar el énfasis en los músculos externos del pecho y los hombros.
Preparación: Coloca las manos en el suelo más separadas que el ancho de los hombros.
Bajada: Desciende hasta que el pecho casi toque el suelo, manteniendo el core firme.
Empuje: Empuja con las palmas para volver a la posición inicial.
Técnica: No dejes que la zona lumbar se hunda; mantén una línea recta desde la cabeza hasta los talones.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Marching High Knees
steps: A low-impact cardio and mobility exercise that strengthens the hip flexors and improves balance.
​Movement: Stand tall and lift one knee toward your chest as high as comfortable.
​Arms: Swing the opposite arm forward as you lift your knee, similar to a walking motion.
​Core: Keep your abs engaged to maintain an upright posture.
​Pace: Perform the movement with control, alternating legs rhythmically.
stepsEs: Un ejercicio de cardio y movilidad de bajo impacto que fortalece los flexores de la cadera y mejora el equilibrio.
Movimiento: Ponte de pie erguido y eleva una rodilla hacia el pecho tan alto como te resulte cómodo.
Brazos: Lleva el brazo contrario hacia delante mientras subes la rodilla, como al caminar.
Core: Mantén los abdominales activados para conservar una postura erguida.
Ritmo: Realiza el movimiento con control, alternando las piernas de forma rítmica.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
steps: Begin in a half kneeling position with the
leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall
with a ball.
With both hands directly in front of
you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach
the wall behind you.
Exhale as you rotate, inhale
as you return to neutral and repeat.
stepsEs: Comienza en posición de media rodilla, con la
pierna alejada de la pared estabilizada contra ella
con una pelota.
Con ambas manos directamente delante
de ti, gira un brazo abriéndolo e intenta alcanzar
la pared que tienes detrás.
Exhala al girar e inhala
al volver a la posición neutra, y repite.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: lento avanti seduto
steps: slow controlled seated forward exercise with dumbbells

name: Single-arm dumbbell shoulder press
nameEs: Press de hombro con mancuerna a un brazo
steps: Press the dumbbell vertically overhead in a controlled motion until your arm is fully extended, without locking the elbow. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.
stepsEs: Presiona la mancuerna verticalmente por encima de la cabeza con un movimiento controlado hasta que el brazo quede completamente extendido, sin bloquear el codo. Baja la mancuerna lentamente de vuelta a la posición inicial a la altura del hombro.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Single-arm cable pushdown
nameEs: Extensión de tríceps en polea a un brazo
steps: Single-arm cable pushdown is a unilateral isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii. By working one arm at a time, it helps correct strength imbalances between sides while also engaging the core for stability.
Starting position:

Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a single handle to the high pulley. Grab the handle with one hand using an overhand grip (pronated), with your elbow bent at approximately 90° and tucked close to your body. Keep your core braced and your back straight.
Execution:
Push the handle downward in a controlled motion by extending your elbow until your arm is fully extended. Hold the contraction for 1 second at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
stepsEs: La extensión de tríceps en polea a un brazo es un ejercicio de aislamiento unilateral que trabaja el tríceps braquial. Al trabajar un brazo a la vez, ayuda a corregir los desequilibrios de fuerza entre ambos lados y, al mismo tiempo, activa el core para mantener la estabilidad.
Posición inicial:

Colócate de pie frente a la máquina de poleas con los pies a la anchura de los hombros. Engancha un asa individual a la polea alta. Agarra el asa con una mano en agarre prono (pronado), con el codo flexionado a unos 90° y pegado al cuerpo. Mantén el core firme y la espalda recta.
Ejecución:

Empuja el asa hacia abajo con un movimiento controlado extendiendo el codo hasta que el brazo quede completamente extendido. Mantén la contracción durante 1 segundo abajo y luego vuelve lentamente a la posición inicial.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Kettlebell sumo high pull
steps: A compound exercise combining elements of a sumo deadlift and a high pull. It targets the posterior chain, particularly the glutes, hamstrings, and upper back. The sumo stance increases hip engagement, while the high pull adds an explosive element, promoting power development.
Stand upright overtop of a kettlebell with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart angled out slightly.
Maintain a braced core and neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Hinge your hips backward and extend your arms to grab ahold the kettlebell with a double overhand grip.
With you lower legs nearly vertical to the ground, extend your hips to raise the kettlebell with your elbows high keeping it close to your body.
Once the kettlebell has reached shoulder height, lower back to the starting position.
stepsEs: Un ejercicio compuesto que combina elementos del peso muerto sumo y del tirón alto (high pull). Trabaja la cadena posterior, en particular los glúteos, los isquiotibiales y la parte alta de la espalda. La postura sumo aumenta la participación de la cadera, mientras que el tirón alto añade un componente explosivo que favorece el desarrollo de la potencia.
Ponte de pie erguido por encima de una kettlebell, con los pies más separados que el ancho de los hombros y las puntas ligeramente hacia afuera.
Mantén el core firme y la columna neutra durante todo el ejercicio.
Lleva la cadera hacia atrás y extiende los brazos para agarrar la kettlebell con un agarre doble prono.
Con las piernas casi verticales respecto al suelo, extiende la cadera para elevar la kettlebell manteniendo los codos altos y la pesa cerca del cuerpo.
Una vez que la kettlebell alcance la altura de los hombros, baja de nuevo a la posición inicial.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Mentzer Pulldown
steps: Close grip front facing Pull down, while focusing on Biceps, Increases activation of biceps over the whole range, Avoid activating Lats.
stepsEs: Jalón al frente con agarre cerrado, centrándote en el bíceps. Aumenta la activación del bíceps en todo el recorrido. Evita activar los dorsales.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
nameEs: Jalón al pecho a un brazo
steps: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and grab the single handle with a neutral grip. Keep your torso stable, your chest lifted, and your shoulder blades slightly retracted. Start with your arm fully extended overhead, then pull the handle down toward your upper chest following a controlled, slightly diagonal path. Focus on engaging the latissimus dorsi while keeping the shoulder depressed and avoiding any torso rotation. Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining full control throughout the movement.
stepsEs: Siéntate en la máquina de jalón y agarra el asa individual con un agarre neutro. Mantén el torso estable, el pecho elevado y las escápulas ligeramente retraídas. Comienza con el brazo completamente extendido por encima de la cabeza y luego tira del asa hacia la parte alta del pecho siguiendo una trayectoria controlada y ligeramente diagonal. Concéntrate en activar el dorsal ancho mientras mantienes el hombro deprimido y evitas cualquier rotación del torso. Vuelve lentamente a la posición inicial, manteniendo el control total durante todo el movimiento.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Hip Airplane
steps: Stand on one leg and lean your upper body slightly forward while keeping your back straight. Extend the free leg behind you so that your torso and leg form roughly one line. Slowly open your hip to the side by rotating your pelvis and upper body in a controlled way. Then close the hip again and return to the starting position.
The movement should mainly come from the hip. Keep your standing foot stable and avoid letting your knee collapse inward.
stepsEs: Ponte de pie sobre una pierna e inclina ligeramente el torso hacia delante mientras mantienes la espalda recta. Extiende la pierna libre hacia atrás de modo que el torso y la pierna formen aproximadamente una línea. Abre la cadera lentamente hacia el lado rotando la pelvis y el torso de forma controlada. Luego cierra la cadera de nuevo y vuelve a la posición inicial.
El movimiento debe provenir principalmente de la cadera. Mantén el pie de apoyo estable y evita que la rodilla se desplome hacia dentro.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Reverse Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your knees stacked on top of each other. Keep your feet together at first, then keep your knees touching while lifting your top foot upward. Slowly lower the foot back down with control.
Move only through the hip and avoid rolling your pelvis backward. The movement should be small, controlled, and focused on hip rotation.
stepsEs: Túmbate de lado con las caderas y las rodillas flexionadas, manteniendo las rodillas apiladas una encima de la otra. Mantén los pies juntos al principio y luego, manteniendo las rodillas en contacto, eleva el pie de arriba hacia arriba. Baja el pie lentamente y con control.
Muévete solo desde la cadera y evita rotar la pelvis hacia atrás. El movimiento debe ser pequeño, controlado y centrado en la rotación de la cadera.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Clamshell to Reverse Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your legs stacked. Lift your top knee into a clamshell position and keep the leg elevated throughout the movement. From there, alternate between opening the knee upward and lifting the foot upward, moving through hip external and internal rotation.
Keep the movement slow and controlled. Do not let the top leg rest on the bottom leg between repetitions.
stepsEs: Túmbate de lado con las caderas y las rodillas flexionadas, manteniendo las piernas apiladas. Eleva la rodilla de arriba a una posición de almeja y mantén la pierna elevada durante todo el movimiento. Desde ahí, alterna entre abrir la rodilla hacia arriba y elevar el pie hacia arriba, pasando por la rotación externa e interna de la cadera.
Mantén el movimiento lento y controlado. No dejes que la pierna de arriba descanse sobre la de abajo entre repeticiones.
instructionCredit: Texto en español de la comunidad de wger; autoría al final de la ficha.

name: Curl De Muñeca Con Barra
steps: This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.
Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders.

Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion.

Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch.

Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second.
Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.
stepsEs: Es un ejercicio de aislamiento diseñado específicamente para desarrollar la masa muscular y la fuerza en la cara interna (anterior) del antebrazo. Es un movimiento clave no solo para la estética del brazo, sino también para mejorar la fuerza de agarre (grip strength), lo que se traduce en un mejor rendimiento en ejercicios pesados como el peso muerto o las dominadas.
Posición Inicial: Toma una barra con un agarre supino (las palmas de las manos mirando hacia arriba) a una anchura similar a la de tus hombros.

Apoyo en el Banco: Arrodíllate frente a un banco plano y apoya la parte posterior de tus antebrazos sobre él. Tus muñecas y manos deben sobresalir ligeramente por el borde del banco para permitir un rango completo de movimiento.

3- Fase Excéntrica (Bajada): Baja la barra de forma controlada extendiendo las muñecas hacia el suelo. Al final del recorrido, abre ligeramente los dedos de las manos para dejar que la barra ruede un poco hacia abajo, maximizando el rango de estiramiento.

Fase Concéntrica (Subida): Cierra primero los dedos para asegurar la barra y luego flexiona las muñecas hacia arriba de forma explosiva pero controlada, llevando la barra lo más alto posible. Contrae con fuerza los antebrazos en la posición máxima durante un segundo.
Postura: Mantén los antebrazos firmemente pegados al banco durante todo el ejercicio; solo deben moverse las muñecas y los dedos.

name: YTW Raises
steps: The YTW exercise for scapular retraction is designed to strengthen the inter-scapular muscles between your shoulder blades, to help retract or pull your shoulders back, helping to maintain proper upright posture.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
steps: Kneel on a glute-ham developer or have a partner hold your ankles. Keeping hips straight, lower your torso toward the floor under control, then curl back up by contracting the hamstrings and glutes.

name: Easy Continuous Swim (Freestyle)
steps: Swim freestyle at a relaxed, steady pace without stopping — think conversation pace, not racing. Focus on smooth, even strokes rather than speed or breathing technique; this is just to get your body moving and your heart rate up.

name: Kick with Board
steps: Hold a kickboard with both hands, arms extended in front of you, face in the water (lift head forward to breathe when needed). Kick from your hips, not your knees, keeping your legs mostly straight with a slight bend and a steady, compact flutter kick. This builds leg endurance and keeps your body horizontal without needing to worry about your arms.

name: Bobbing Exhale Drill
steps: Stand in chest-deep water. Take a breath, submerge your face fully, and exhale slowly and completely through your nose and/or mouth the whole time you're underwater — a gentle humming sound can help keep the exhale steady and controlled. Once you're empty of air, lift your head, take a fresh breath, and go back under. Repeat continuously. The goal is training your body that all your exhaling happens underwater, so all you need to do at the surface is inhale.

name: Wall-Hold Rotation
steps: Hold the pool wall or edge with one hand, body horizontal at the surface, legs kicking gently behind you. Keep your face in the water, exhaling continuously, then rotate your head to the side — not lifting it up — so one goggle stays in the water while the other clears the surface. Take a quick breath, then rotate your face back down to neutral. This isolates the head-rotation motion without any arm strokes to think about.

name: Side-Kick Breathing (Kickboard)
steps: Push off the wall on your side (not flat on your stomach), one arm extended forward holding the board or just extended, kicking continuously. Keep your head in a neutral position looking at the bottom of the pool, and when you need air, rotate your head sideways (one ear stays in the water, other faces up) to breathe, then rotate back to neutral. Swim a length like this, then repeat on the other side. This teaches the exact head position and rotation you'll use once full stroke breathing comes in.

name: Stroke-and-Roll Drill
steps: Push off, swim a few strokes, and every breath roll fully onto your back for 2-3 breaths, then roll back into freestyle. This teaches you to rotate your body as a unit rather than just turning your head, and helps remove the fear of not having your face in the water.

name: Recovery Bobbing
steps: Same motion as the Bobbing Exhale Drill, but done in slightly deeper water (so you're not touching the bottom) and at a slower, more relaxed pace — think of it as a recovery/reset exercise rather than a hard drill. Use it between harder drills to reset your breathing rhythm and calm down if you're feeling rushed or out of sync.

name: Cool-Down Swim
steps: Swim at an easy, unhurried pace — freestyle, backstroke, or just floating/gliding — with zero focus on technique or drills. The only goal here is to let your heart rate come down gradually and your muscles relax before you get out of the pool.

name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Flatten your lower back against the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, engaging your abs and glutes. Hold 5 seconds, release. This retrains pelvic positioning to counter anterior pelvic tilt.
aliases: Pelvic Tilt Drill / Supine Pelvic Tilt

name: Band Terminal Knee extension
steps: This is an end range strengthening exercise for the knee extensors. Start by looping a band around the back of one knee and anchoring the other end to a stable surface in front of you. Stand in a split stance with the banded knee bent and placed as the front leg. Straighten the knee to pull against the bands resistance and maintain a contraction in your quadriceps for up to 5 seconds before releasing.

name: Serratus Wall Slide Stretch
steps: Stand facing a wall. Place your forearms vertically against the wall so your elbows and wrists are both touching it.
Point your arms slightly outwards from "straight up".
Protract your shoulders had, then slide your forearms up the wall until your elbows are about level with your chin.
Slide your forearms back down the wall. Repeat as necessary.

name: Couch Stretch
steps: Stand facing away from a bench, couch or similar-height object.
Extend one leg backwards, resting your foot "laces-down" on the edge of the bench.
Lower yourself until your rear knee is on the floor and you are in a lunge position, with your torso hanging forwards slightly.
Brace your core, tense your rear glute, and straighten up your torso to vertical, under control. Relax and repeat.
Repeat for the other leg, too.

name: Long Lunge Pulse Stretch
steps: Hold the resistance band (or any other rope-like object, the elasticity is not necessary) above your head, between your hands, with your arms straight. Pull it taught to engage your lats.
Step forwards into a lunge, dropping until your knee is almost touching the floor.
Slowly and controlledly pulse your body up and down by about an inch. Repeat for required reps.
Repeat for other leg.

name: Front Split Stretch
steps: Start kneeling.
Extend one leg out forwards, fully straightened. Follow with your hips so your back leg begins to unfold.
Carefully lower yourself into the stretch. Do not go beyond your limit.
Hold for the required time.

name: Squat Sky Reach Stretch
steps: Drop into a squat.
Hold one ankle with the opposite hand.
Fold your other arm to your chest.
Staying in the squat and keeping hold of your ankle, twist to turn your chest-hand back/outwards until your elbow is pointing at the sky.
Return to the neutral squatting position with your hand on your chest. Repeat movement as required.
Repeat on both sides.

name: explosive push ups
steps: Explosive Push-Ups
Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

name: Russian Push Ups
steps: Russian Push-Ups

Start in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift your body forward while keeping your chest close to the ground. Extend your arms to return to the starting position, then reverse the movement smoothly. Keep your core tight and maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise.

name: elbow lever
steps: ​A calisthenics static balance skill where the entire body is held straight and parallel to the ground, supported by tucking the elbows firmly into the abdomen or pelvic bones.

name: Planche Lean Hold
steps: A straight-arm calisthenics static hold where you assume a plank position and lean the shoulders as far forward as possible past the wrists with protracted scapulae and a hollow body.

name: Arch Hang
steps: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C995b3KLXS4&t=7s
Elbows should stay straight
Hold it for time/reps
Start at an active hang: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HoE-C85ZlCE
Progress towards a 90 degree in your shoulder

name: Leg Extension Isometric
steps: An isometric leg extension is a strengthening exercise where you contract your quadriceps muscles against an immovable resistance without changing the length of the muscle or moving your knee joint.

name: Bench Press Isometric
steps: A bench press isometric hold is a static strength exercise where you pause and hold a barbell or dumbbells either at your chest, mid-press, or at lockout without moving for a set time

name: Overhead Press Isometric
steps: An isometric overhead press involves holding a weight statically overhead or pushing against an immovable object at a specific point in the press without moving the joint.

name: Lateral Raise Isometric
steps: An isometric lateral raise is a shoulder exercise where you hold your arms out to the sides at waist height for a set amount of time instead of moving up and down

name: Preacher Curl Isometric
steps: An isometric preacher curl is a static strength exercise where you hold a fixed position on a preacher pad or and inclined bench under tension without moving the joint.

name: Lat Pulldown Isometric
steps: An isometric Lat pulldown is a strength-building exercise where you pull the bar down to your chest and hold the contracted position at the bottom without moving your limbs for a set number of seconds

name: Triceps Pushdown Isometric
steps: A single-arm isometric or isolated triceps pushdown is an isolation cable exercise where you pin your upper arm against your torso, hinge at the hips, and extend the elbow to achieve a peak contraction in the triceps muscle.

name: Boxing
steps: Bag workout for boxing skill development and cardio improvement

name: Wrist circles
steps: Wrist circles is warm-up exercise, where you rotate your wrists in a circular motion. They improve mobility and are recommended before exercises such as pull ups, hand stands and other exercises that put pressure on your wrists.

name: Retro Treadmill Walking
steps: Controlled treadmill walking performed backward. Begin around 30 minutes at a controlled speed and approximately 2 to 3 percent incline if tolerated. Progress duration gradually as knee, hip, and back tolerance improves.

name: Kegel Exercise
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit upright in a chair. Locate the pelvic floor muscles: they are the muscles you would use to stop the flow of urine or to hold back gas. Keep your abdomen, glutes and thighs relaxed and breathe normally throughout.

Tighten the pelvic floor muscles and lift them gently upwards and inwards. Hold the contraction for a few seconds, then release completely and rest for at least as long as you held. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
The exercise can be varied by holding longer with a light contraction (endurance) or by performing quick, short contractions with a full relaxation in between.

name: Supported Split Squat
steps: Supported split squat performed with stable balance support and controlled depth.

name: 90/90 Breathing
steps: Controlled breathing drill performed in a 90/90 position to encourage rib, abdominal, and pelvic coordination.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor.

Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

name: Adductor Rock Backs
steps: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward.

Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs.
Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.

name: Elevated Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand facing a bar, box or bench at roughly hip height and place the heel of one leg on it. Keep that leg straight with the toes pointing up, and keep the standing leg straight with both hips square to the support.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch in the back of the elevated thigh. Hold the position while breathing calmly, then switch legs.
Stretch for the hamstrings. The height of the support controls the intensity: the higher the leg, the stronger the stretch.

name: Single-leg BOSU balance
steps: Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise

The exercise for balancing on a BOSU ball while standing on one leg is known as the single-leg BOSU balance exercise. This exercise is effective for enhancing balance, coordination, and core stability.
Benefits of the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Improves Balance: Standing on one leg challenges your stability.
Enhances Coordination: Engaging different muscle groups helps improve overall coordination.
Strengthens Core: The exercise activates core muscles, promoting better posture and stability.
How to Perform the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Positioning: Stand on the dome side of the BOSU ball with one leg.
Balance: Keep your opposite leg lifted and your core engaged.
Duration: Aim to hold the position for 10-20 seconds, gradually increasing the time as you improve.
Progression Tips
Add Movement: Try reaching for objects around you while maintaining balance.
Close Your Eyes: This increases the challenge by removing visual stability cues.
Use a Ball: Catch or toss a ball while balancing to further engage your core and coordination.
This exercise is a great way to build foundational balance skills before progressing to more complex movements.

name: Quad Sets
steps: What Are Quad Sets?

Quad sets are a fundamental exercise used in knee rehabilitation. They focus on strengthening the quadriceps muscles located at the front of the thigh. This exercise is particularly beneficial for individuals recovering from knee injuries or surgeries.
How to Perform Quad Sets
Steps to Execute Quad Sets
Positioning: Sit or lie down with your legs straight.
Tightening: Tighten the quadriceps muscles while keeping the leg straight. You should see the kneecap move upward.
Holding: Maintain the contraction for about 5 seconds.
Releasing: Relax the muscle after the hold.
Repetitions: Aim for 10 to 15 repetitions, gradually increasing as strength improves.
Tips for Effective Quad Sets
Ensure no other muscles are contracting to assist the quadriceps.
Perform the exercise on a flat surface, like a bed or couch, with a towel or pillow under your heel for comfort.
It is recommended to do these exercises multiple times a day, especially during the early stages of recovery.
Benefits of Quad Sets
Restores Muscle Function: Helps rebuild strength in the quadriceps.
Improves Stability: Enhances stability in the knee joint.
Increases Range of Motion: Aids in regaining mobility after injury or surgery.
Incorporating quad sets into your rehabilitation routine can significantly aid in recovery and improve overall knee function.

name: Hip-Out and Hip-In Lateral Steps
steps: Overview of Hip-Out and Hip-In Lateral Steps

Hip-out and hip-in lateral steps are effective exercises designed to strengthen the hip abductors and enhance lateral stability. These movements are beneficial for improving coordination and overall hip function.
Exercise Descriptions
Hip-Out Steps
Movement: Step out to the side with one leg, keeping the other leg stable.
Target Muscles: Primarily engages the hip abductors, including the gluteus medius and minimus.
Benefits: Increases lateral stability and strength in the hip area.
Hip-In Steps
Movement: Bring the leg back in toward the center after stepping out.
Target Muscles: Continues to engage the hip abductors while also activating the adductors.
Benefits: Enhances coordination and control of the hip joint.
Key Benefits of Lateral Steps
| Benefit | Description |
| Strengthening Hip Abductors | Improves muscle strength around the hip joint. |
| Enhancing Stability | Increases lateral stability, reducing the risk of falls. |
| Improving Coordination | Develops better control and movement patterns in the hips. |
Incorporating hip-out and hip-in lateral steps into a regular exercise routine can lead to improved hip strength and stability, which is essential for various physical activities and daily movements.

name: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
steps: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds

Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises that focus on balance and stability by landing softly on one leg and holding the position. This exercise helps improve proprioception and can be beneficial for rehabilitation and athletic training.
Overview

Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises designed to enhance balance, stability, and proprioception. They involve landing softly on one leg and maintaining that position for a brief period. This exercise is particularly useful in rehabilitation settings and for athletes looking to improve their performance.
Benefits
Improves balance: Enhances stability by training the body to control weight distribution on one leg.
Enhances proprioception: Increases awareness of body position, which is crucial for injury prevention.
Supports rehabilitation: Helps individuals recover from lower-limb injuries by strengthening muscles and improving joint stability.
How to Perform Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
Steps
Preparation: Stand on a stable surface or a box.
Takeoff: Step off the box or surface with one leg, ensuring that you do not jump.
Landing: Land softly on the target leg, allowing the knee and hip to bend slightly.
Hold position: Maintain balance in the landed position for up to 2 seconds.
Reset: Return to the starting position and repeat.
Key Points to Remember
Keep your chest up and engage your core for better stability.
Ensure your knee aligns with the midline of your foot during landing.
Focus on a controlled descent to minimize impact.
Conclusion

Incorporating single-leg soft-landing holds into your training routine can significantly enhance your balance and stability, making it a valuable exercise for both rehabilitation and athletic performance.

name: Reverse V-Squat
steps: Step into the V-squat machine facing the pad, the opposite way from the regular V-squat, so that your chest rests against the pad and your shoulders sit under the shoulder pads. Place your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart and release the safety.

Brace your core and lower yourself by bending your knees and pushing the hips back until your thighs are roughly parallel to the platform. Drive back up through the heels without locking out the knees.
Compared to the regular V-squat, the reversed position shifts the emphasis towards the glutes and hamstrings.

name: Box Handstand Push-up
steps: Pike push-up with legs on an elevated surface. Progression to handstand push-up.

name: Banded Front Raise
steps: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet about hip-width apart, holding one end in each hand in front of your thighs. Keeping your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows, raise your hands forward to shoulder height, then lower slowly under control. Can be done with both arms together or alternating. Use a heavier band or shorten the band to increase resistance.

name: Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown
steps: Sit at a plate-loaded (lever) lat pulldown machine with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the handles overhead with arms fully extended. Pull the handles down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your lats at the bottom. Return slowly to full extension. Resistance comes from weight plates loaded on the machine's lever arms rather than a cable stack.

name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise
steps: Set a cable pulley at the lowest position and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine, hold the frame with your near hand and lean your body away so you hang at an angle. With the far hand, grasp the handle in front of your hips and raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow. Lower slowly. The lean increases tension on the side delts at the bottom of the movement. Complete all reps, then switch sides.

name: Seated Band Row
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you and your back tall. Loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet and hold one end in each hand, arms extended and a slight bend in the knees. Pull the band toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows straight back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your chest up and your torso still rather than rocking backward to move the band. Extend the arms slowly to return. Because the torso stays upright and supported, this is a useful row when a bent-over position is uncomfortable, and it needs no anchor point.

name: FlexBar Wrist Extension
steps: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing down and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist drop, then extend the wrist to raise the bar, keeping the forearm still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. The resistance comes from twisting or bending the flexible bar, so a thicker or stiffer bar increases the load. Commonly used for wrist and forearm strengthening and for elbow tendon rehabilitation.

name: FlexBar Wrist Flexion
steps: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist extend back, then curl the wrist up to raise the bar while the forearm stays still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. Works the wrist flexors, and is the companion movement to FlexBar wrist extension for balanced forearm strengthening.

name: FlexBar Tyler Twist
steps: An eccentric exercise for the wrist extensors, done with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar, and widely used in rehabilitation for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Hold the bar vertically in the affected hand with the wrist extended. Grasp the top of the bar with the other hand, palm facing away, and twist the top hand to wind up the bar. Bring both arms out in front of you with the bar horizontal, then slowly let the affected wrist untwist the bar over about four seconds while the other hand holds steady. Reset and repeat. The reverse version, twisting in the opposite direction for the wrist flexors, is used for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). Move slowly and stop if the exercise causes sharp pain rather than the expected mild discomfort.

name: Paused Squats
steps: Use the same technic as your normal squat. Except that you make a pause at the bottom of the squat for about 1-2 seconds, in other words a bit longer than your normal squat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row /w Rotation (floor)
steps: Go into a one-legged kneeling position and grab the cable from the lowest position.
Rotate the upper torso to get into the starting position and bend the upper torso a little bit sidewise.
Place the unused hand on the knee.
Pull the cable while rotating the upper torso.

name: Seated Knee Extension with Overpressure
steps: A gentle stretch to restore full knee extension. Sit with one leg stretched out in front of you and the heel propped on the floor or a low surface, so the knee is unsupported. Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap. Keeping the leg relaxed, gently press down through the hands toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee, and hold for about three seconds before releasing. The pressure should produce a stretch, never sharp pain. Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Banded Monster Walk
steps: A banded walking drill for the glutes and hip stabilisers. Place a mini band around both thighs just above the knees, or around the ankles for a harder version. Stand with feet hip-width apart so the band is under tension, then sink into a quarter-squat with the chest up. Walk forward with small diagonal steps, pushing each leg out against the band and keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than letting them fall inward. Walk forward for the prescribed number of steps, then walk backward to return, keeping the band under tension throughout.

name: Step Calf Stretch
steps: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Eyes Closed
steps: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Kettlebell Circles
steps: A balance drill that adds a moving load. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand. Pass the kettlebell around your body in a circle, handing it from one hand to the other in front and behind you, while keeping your balance on the standing leg. Keep the hips level and the torso upright; the shifting weight of the bell constantly changes your centre of mass, which is what trains the hip and ankle stabilisers. Complete the prescribed number of circles, reverse direction, then switch legs. Use a light bell to start.
aliases: Kettlebell Body Circle on One Leg

name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rows (Two Arms)
steps: How to Perform It
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral or overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back, until your torso is roughly 45–75 degrees to the floor. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders with arms fully extended.
Keep your back flat, chest up, and core braced — avoid rounding your spine.
Pull the dumbbells up toward your ribcage/hips, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Key Coaching Cues
Hinge from the hips, not the lower back
Keep the spine neutral throughout — no rounding
Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Avoid using momentum or jerking the weight up
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase rather than letting the weights drop

name: Alternate Walking
steps: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat

name: Radio Taiso
steps: Video can be found here : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGPBSqxKGAc
Full-body mobility and dynamic warm-up routine (3–5 minutes) to prepare joints, muscles, and the cardiovascular system for workout.
Movement Flow:
Deep Breathing & Arm Raises: Inhale while raising arms laterally overhead, exhale as you lower them.
Knee Bends: Soft, rhythmic knee flexions synchronized with arm swings.
Arm Circles: Large full-range arm rotations forward, then backward to open up the chest and shoulder girdle.
Chest Expansion: Cross arms in front of the chest and open wide to the sides.
Side Bends: Reach overhead to stretch the lateral torso left and right with a smooth side flexion.
Forward & Back Bends: Gently hinge at the hips to reach forward, then return upright with a mild spinal extension.
Torso Twists: Swing arms side-to-side to rotate the spine and loosen the core.
Ankle Mobility / Light Bounces: Soft heel lifts or light bouncing on toes to warm up lower leg joints and tendons.

name: kelso shrugs
steps: Kelso shrugs are a variation of scapular shrugs designed primarily to train scapular retraction , with particular emphasis on the middle trapezius, rhomboids, and, secondarily, the lower trapezius . Unlike conventional shrugs, the goal is not to elevate the shoulders toward the ears, but rather to pull the shoulder blades backward .
They are typically performed with the chest supported on an incline bench, using either dumbbells or a barbell:
Lie face down on an incline bench, with your arms extended toward the floor.
Keep your elbows almost completely locked throughout the movement.
Starting with the shoulder blades slightly protracted, retract them , trying to bring them closer together.
Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench; avoid turning the movement into a row by extending your torso.
Briefly hold the fully retracted position, then return in a controlled manner, allowing the shoulder blades to separate.
stepsEs: Los Kelso shrugs son una variante de encogimiento escapular diseñada para trabajar principalmente la retracción de las escápulas, con especial énfasis en el trapecio medio, romboides y, secundariamente, trapecio inferior. A diferencia de un shrug convencional, no buscas elevar los hombros hacia las orejas, sino llevar las escápulas hacia atrás.
Se suelen realizar apoyando el pecho sobre un banco inclinado, con mancuernas o barra:
Colócate boca abajo sobre un banco inclinado, con los brazos extendidos hacia el suelo.
Mantén los codos prácticamente bloqueados durante todo el movimiento.
Desde una posición en la que las escápulas estén ligeramente protraídas, retráelas, intentando acercarlas entre sí.
El pecho permanece apoyado: no debes convertir el ejercicio en un remo extendiendo el tronco.
Mantén brevemente la máxima retracción y vuelve de forma controlada permitiendo que las escápulas se separen.

name: Stomach Vacuum
steps: Starting position : Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor (or stand/sit upright).
Exhalation : Fully exhale all the air from your lungs through your mouth.
Contraction : Draw your navel in towards your spine as far as possible, pulling your stomach inward and up under your ribcage.
Hold : Hold this isometric contraction without breathing for 10 to 20 seconds.
Release : Slowly inhale through your nose to release the tension and relax your abdominals.
Repeat : Rest briefly and perform the desired number of sets.

name: Weighted neck flexion
steps: Weighted neck flexion is an isolation exercise designed to strengthen the anterior (front) neck flexor muscles by bringing your chin toward your chest against external resistance (most commonly a light weight plate, resistance band, or neck harness).

name: Single leg press
steps: Strength training exercise where you push a weight away from your body using one leg at a time on a leg press machine. It helps to improve leg strength, balance, and muscular symmetry by isolating each leg individually. This exercise is particularly useful for identifying and correcting muscle imbalances between your legs.
